The *Aṅkolapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 367) is a biographical verse text preserved in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The poem recounts the past meritorious deeds of the elder (thera) associated with an offering of *aṅkola* flowers. Five modern translations across five languages are cataloged on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are identified for this text [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus records considerable Pali-internal text reuse, identifying 39 matching segments shared with 19 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The initial verses (§0.3–3.3) are closely aligned with a passage in the first part of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (§4584–4589) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, the text shares standard formulaic verses (§3.1–6.1) with numerous other flower-offering poems in the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Uddālakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 369), two poems titled *Saḷalapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 270 and Tha-Ap 372), the *Ticampakapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 256), and the *Piyālapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 239) [DharmaNexus].
